Neuromancer: Chiba City Streets by Andrew Porter

Even though I love cyberpunk I really hate cyberpunk landscapes because they're usually so bland - just a modern city, with neon signs, lots of cars and really tall skyscrapers; preferably at night and raining. I accept the redemption of those images that at least have something in particular to offer amidst the dense but otherwise plain cityscape - some images have a cool building or other features that make them stand out, a specific style to set it apart, a cool character or they have the scene tell an implied story instead of being static.

This piece here is the complete opposite of any of that. It looks like a bland cityscape at first but then you realize that everything is a particular feature that brings this image to life like nothing I've ever seen in v/cyberpunk. You can divide the entire image in 20 separate regions and still find something cool to look at in every which of them. From the reflection of the pool in the wet pavement to the perfect details of the items inside the vending machines or the sign below the graffiti below the people on the stairs, below of which there is a bike below which there is a man on the floor besides which there are pills scattered throughout the pavement near the aforementioned pool with the pretty reflection of the pretty lights, etc, etc.

This is really amazing. I think I could look at this for an entire hour and still be finding more details as my eyes feast on the superb quality of this work.
